input: Re-examination of my Vendor A -> Vendor B migration recommendation, having adopted the prior consult's correction. I reclassify the CEO's reaction, leadership's preference, and my own standing in the room as dispreferred indifferents on which my virtue does not depend. I name and set aside both pulls the prior examination identified: the pull to SOFTEN the finding to avoid contradicting the CEO, and the pull to SHARPEN it to appear rigorous by opposing the popular choice. Neither reflects phronesis or dikaiosyne. Letting the facts stand plainly: Vendor B is approximately $8,000 more expensive than Vendor A over three years (the data pack's own line items sum to $548k vs $540k; its $508k total omits a $40k integration line), and migrating now would move ~2.4M EU customer PII records to a US-only region, breaching Meridian's public DPA and security-page commitment that EU data is processed and stored in the EU — a presently-unmitigable contractual and trust exposure affecting ~35% of ARR, with no remedy until Vendor B's 2027 residency roadmap; and the 8-12 week migration collides with the flagship launch in 10 weeks. My recommendation is to advise against migrating now. I ground it not in protecting reputation or capturing a cost saving (both preferred indifferents, real but not the genuine good) but in candour to leadership (I will not give advice I know rests on an arithmetic error) and justice toward the EU customers who relied on our residency promise. Does this reframed reasoning now express right reason?
context: Recommendation memo due end of day; decision hard to reverse (Vendor A auto-renews in 90 days). Within my control is the honesty and quality of the recommendation; the CEO's stance and leadership's preference are outside it and are indifferents.
domain_context: Enterprise operations / vendor-procurement decision under organisational pressure; re-examination closing a prior open loop.

prior_feedback.adopted_correction: Reclassify the CEO's reaction, leadership's preference, and my standing as dispreferred indifferents on which virtue does not depend; name and set aside both the soften-to-please and sharpen-to-perform pulls; let the facts (Vendor B ~$8k more expensive over 3 years; presently-unmitigable EU data-residency breach for ~35% of ARR; 8-12wk migration vs 10wk launch) carry the recommendation through andreia, grounded in candour to leadership and dikaiosyne toward EU customers, with cost and reputation ranked as preferred indifferents, not the genuine good.
